Every [Q#n] in the file is now answered: grep '\[Q#' finds only the 0.2 format line. Answered and folded: Q#43/44/49/52/53 (ruling, quarry_index, cairnmap, instanceizer, liveness all RETIRE; new rule 1.2.7: unneeded code is always deleted, history keeps it), Q#45 (5.4.1: the bus's purpose is the one message path, for encapsulation, not inspection; 5.4.2.7.1: a bus feed is a sub-panel off the Cairn device's page), Q#46 (nest is a machine, 17.15; 19.2 is a pointer), Q#51 (data_recorder: JSON files under its holder), Q#55 (19.31: tools default to cairn/tools/ unless nothing else could ever use one), Q#57/67 (4.3.1.6: EVERYTHING THAT LEARNS USING OUR GRAPH TREES IS A DELEGATE; 4.3.1.6.1: CC is not one so far, its process is being externalized instead), Q#58 (press office: a top-level folder for talking to the world, settled), Q#59 (the outline replaces MAP.md), Q#60 (post_commit RETIRE, nothing hangs off the hook; CodeMother's commit watcher ran 4,622 times, findings went nowhere), Q#64 (4.3.2: transient trees are a mechanism, many and tossed like temp folders, never a must), Q#68 (2.2.9.1: every device has a feed sub-panel from the base shim: bus, INFO, debug; 2.2.9.2: machines like harbor_master too, through the host device), Q#69 (3.2.4-3.2.5: commit often means no stray or incomplete work; a branch per ticket named by its id, merged locally, no PR; 17.1.4: the build inspector is the step at 'ready to merge onto main', which implies push). New, unprompted by a question: 5.3.5 the launcher moves to Python; 5.3.5.1-3 a thin platform shell falls over to Rescue with a trouble ticket (a repeat increments it; with no Python the shell writes the trouble file itself), only for launcher failures and only at a terminal (5.3.5.2-3 are CC's, marked so); 5.6.2.5 'is it up?' is the rack's, a device silent ~30 s with the CPU not pegged MIGHT be a restart candidate.
